title: Choosing a beach, and the rules that go with it

p: The Grand Strand is about 60 miles of continuous beach, and it feels different from one end to the other. Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach (with Cherry Grove) are the liveliest, with piers, boardwalks and restaurants close to the sand. Surfside Beach and Garden City are more family-oriented, with a slower pace and a long pier at Garden City. Litchfield and Pawleys Island are the quiet ones, with fewer crowds and more houses than hotels.

Each town sets its own beach rules, so what is allowed in North Myrtle Beach may not be allowed in Myrtle Beach or Pawleys Island. Here is what the official sources say in general. Check your town's page before you go, because rules change.

Alcohol and glass containers are prohibited on most public beaches in the area. Open fires and grills are generally banned. Tent and canopy rules vary: North Myrtle Beach bars tents and cabanas from mid-May through Labor Day, while umbrellas are allowed, and Pawleys Island permits open-sided tents with the rule that holes are filled in. Dogs are allowed during certain hours that change by season and town, and must be leashed.

From May 1 through October 31 many beach towns also have lights-out rules to protect nesting sea turtles. Beachfront lights go off at night, and you should fill in holes and take your gear with you at the end of the day. Fines can run up to $500, so it is worth reading the signs.

list: Sunscreen, water and a shade plan that fits the local rule.
A bag to carry out your trash.
A flat-bottomed cart or a light bag if you have a long walk from the access point or parking.
A plan for parking. Beach access parking varies by town and season, and meters are common in busy areas.
